sections.title: Coverage snapshot
sections.content: Before: 3443 tests / 244 files, 0 fail. After: 3479 tests / 248 files, 0 fail. Full-suite run confirms no regressions.

sections.title: Gaps closed (real tests, not stubs)
sections.content:
| File | Funcs before → after | What was untested |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/error-capture.ts` | 0% → 100% | The out-of-band capture buffer `src/server.ts` reads to recover a stack when h3 swallows a 500 (CLAUDE.md flags this file as load-bearing). No test drove the global `error`/`unhandledrejection` listeners, the single-consume semantics, or the 5s TTL expiry. |
| `src/lib/error-page.ts` | 0% → 100% | The catastrophic-500 fallback HTML. No regression guard existed against a future change accidentally leaking a stack trace into that page. |
| `src/lib/a2a-card.ts` | 0% → 100% | The A2A/MCP discovery contract served at `/.well-known/agent.json`. Untested meant a broken endpoint URL or a scope typo would ship silently to every peer agent that discovers Cadence. |
| `src/lib/knowledge-graph-view.functions.ts` | 0% → 20% | Two pure helpers, `isMissingColumnError` (the 42703 pre-migration probe) and `chunk` (PostgREST `.in()` batching), were doing real branching but were module-private, so nothing could reach them. I exported both (additive, no behavior change) and tested them directly. |

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
`error-capture.ts` is a good example of testing module-singleton state without reaching into internals: dispatch the real `ErrorEvent`/`unhandledrejection` on `globalThis` (the same path production code fires), then assert through the public `consumeLastCapturedError()`. For the TTL test, monkey-patching `Date.now` after the capture (not before) is what makes it deterministic — the capture timestamp is real, only the *read* time is faked forward past the 5s window, then restored in a `finally`.

The `knowledge-graph-view.functions.ts` case shows the codebase's actual testability convention in action: files like `discover/format.ts`, `discover/ranking.ts`, and `decisions-shared.ts` all exist because someone deliberately pulled pure logic out of a `.functions.ts` server module into a sibling file. Here the same pure logic was still inline and just needed `export` — smallest possible fix to make it directly testable.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

sections.title: A latent bug found while writing the `chunk` tests
sections.content: `chunk(arr, size)` uses `for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += size)`. If `size` is ever `0`, that's an infinite loop. Every current call site passes the hardcoded constant `IN_BATCH = 25`, so it's unreachable today — I did **not** add a test for `chunk(arr, 0)` (it would hang the suite) and did not add a guard, since nothing calls it that way. Flagging it rather than silently skipping, per the "no silent caps" rule: if `chunk` is ever exposed to a caller-supplied batch size, it needs a `size > 0` guard first.

sections.title: Remaining gaps I did NOT write tests for, and why
sections.content:
**Cluster 1 — `.functions.ts` server modules with no pure-logic extraction** (`today.functions.ts` 5.9%, `outcome.functions.ts` 10.6%, `pm-impact.functions.ts` 18.4%, `feedback.functions.ts` 13.1%, `playbooks.functions.ts` 30.4%, `calendar-connections.functions.ts` 16.3%, `profile.functions.ts` 34.9%, `onboarding.functions.ts` 7.0%, `ask-canvas.functions.ts` 8.1%, `decisions.functions.ts` 7.5%, `discovery.functions.ts` 6.8%). I checked each — unlike `knowledge-graph-view.functions.ts`, these have no separable pure branching; the logic is interleaved directly with `createServerFn`/Supabase calls. Closing this properly means the same "extract to a sibling `-shared.ts`" refactor the codebase already applies elsewhere — that's a design change, not a test-writing task, so I'm flagging it rather than doing it unprompted.

**Cluster 2 — connector provider adapters** (`stripe.server.ts`, `salesforce.server.ts`, `hubspot.server.ts`, `canny.server.ts`, `zendesk.server.ts`, `intercom.server.ts`, `productboard.server.ts`, `github.server.ts`, `gmail-ingest.server.ts`, `outlook-mail-ingest.server.ts`, `slack.server.ts`, `bearer.server.ts`) — all 0–27% funcs. These need mocked HTTP/OAuth responses per provider; that's integration-test territory (the repo's own `ecc:e2e-runner` agent is the right tool), not unit skeletons.

**Cluster 3 — AI runtime internals** (`memory.server.ts`, `critic.server.ts`, `prompts.server.ts`, `assumptions.server.ts`, `governing-decision.server.ts`, `reflection.server.ts`, `shared-premise.server.ts`, `platform-keys.server.ts`, `edge-extractor.server.ts`, `json-shape.ts`, `eval-gate.ts`) — all near 0%. These sit behind the `runtime.server.ts` chokepoint and need the model call mocked; also integration territory.

**Cluster 4 — small pure-JSX components at 0%** (`AutoChip.tsx`, `PanelSkeleton.tsx`, `ArrivalButterfly.tsx`, 20–30 lines each) — no branching logic, just markup. Per the skill's own guidance, this is denominator noise, not a real gap; a render-only snapshot test wouldn't catch real regressions.

No suite ran long enough to need backgrounding, and nothing above was silently dropped — it's categorized so the next pass knows exactly where to start.
